title: Priority dampening + autoscaler probe window leak causing reserved-pool depletion during cross-region surge
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description: Summary: During a multi-region traffic surge on 2026-03-09 we observed several customers on Dedicated capacity report elevated 429s and large latency spikes. The reserved pools backing those tenants were drained rapidly and autoscaler did not provision fallback capacity fast enough. This ticket tracks the diagnosis, temporary mitigations, the permanent fix, and follow-up hardening work.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Create two Dedicated tenant reservations in us-west1 and europe-west3 with small reserved pool headroom (1-2 GPUs).
2) Schedule a synthetic workload that emits microbursts (100-300 concurrent short requests) from both regions such that traffic synchronizes into a 90s window.
3) Observe allocator headroom telemetry and autoscaler probe windows.
4) Confirm that tenant-priority dampening reduces weight quicker than probes can detect capacity pressure, leading to early burst token consumption and no global fallback until headroom reaches 0.
observed_behavior:
- Rapid depletion of burst credits and reserved slots within 60-120s.
- Autoscaler probe window (probe_interval_ms + probe_backoff) failed to trigger an early scale-up due to probe aggregation bug.
- Fallback routing to compatible model variants/regions did not fire because per-tenant capacity estimate cache remained stale for up to 5 minutes.
- Affected customers saw elevated 429s and 2–8x latency increases for short requests.
impact_summary: Impacted 7 paying Dedicated tenants across multiple accounts (finance, healthcare, and SaaS customers). Incidents lasted between 2–8 minutes before on-call manual intervention restored service for high-priority tenants. Estimated business impact: short-term SLA degradation, three customer escalations (one opened a P1 support case).
mitigation_taken:
- 2026-03-09 17:42 UTC: Temporarily disabled aggressive priority dampening for affected region feature toggle (feature:priority_dampening_v2).
- 2026-03-09 17:50 UTC: Forced cache refresh of per-tenant capacity estimates and bumped probe sampling frequency for the autoscaler (hotfix toggle:autoscaler_probe_frequency).
- 2026-03-09 18:05 UTC: Raised reserved pool safety headroom for critical tenants by +40% through emergency config override.
- Communicated to customers with an incident summary and ETA for permanent fix.
root_cause_analysis:
Multiple interacting issues produced the outage: 
1) Priority dampening algorithm: a recent change introduced a multiplicative dampening factor that applied to both steady-state weight and burst token accounting. When two regions emitted synchronized microbursts the dampening multiplier aggressively reduced per-tenant fairness tokens, increasing the rate at which burst credit was consumed.
2) Probe aggregation bug: the autoscaler probe scheduler aggregated probe responses across edge-nodes and erroneously dropped probe events when more than 16 concurrent probes were in-flight, due to an off-by-one in the probe bucket ring buffer. This delayed detection of sustained pressure for the allocated pool.
3) Stale capacity-estimate cache: a 300s TTL introduced during an unrelated perf change prevented fallback routing from seeing the most recent headroom numbers. The fallback logic requires fresh capacity_estimate_age < 30s to trigger region/model failover.
Individually these would be minor; combined they allowed fast depletion without timely scale or fallback.
fix_summary:
- Reverted the dampening multiplier change and introduced a capped additive dampening to keep burst accounting decoupled (PR: github.com/redwood/allocator/pull/4892).
- Fixed probe bucket ring buffer off-by-one and added defensive metrics for dropped probes (PR: github.com/redwood/autoscaler/pull/1209).
- Reset capacity-estimate TTL back to 30s and added a cache-invalidation hook when allocation decisions change (PR: github.com/redwood/routing/pull/334).
All three PRs are in review; unit + integration tests added to cover synchronized microburst scenarios.
rollout_plan:
1) Merge PRs behind feature gates and deploy to staging (runtime-1.21-staging) for 48h of synthetic microburst validation.
2) Canary deploy to us-west1-eu small percentage (5% traffic, 2 hours) with throttled ramp-up. Monitor: reserved-pool headroom, probe-drop-rate, capacity_cache_age.
3) If metrics stable for 2h, increase to 25% then 100% over 12h.
4) Post-rollout: keep priority_dampening_v2 disabled for 72h and evaluate.
Rollout owner: Ethan Chen. Backout plan: revert merges and re-enable temporary mitigations (cache refresh/probe frequency) documented above.
monitoring_and_metrics:
Dashboards and alerts updated: 
- dashboard: Reserved Pool Headroom (per-tenant) -> alert if headroom < 10% for > 30s.
- autoscaler_probes: probe_drop_rate (new metric) -> alert if > 0.5% sustained.
- capacity_estimate_age -> alert if > 60s.
- customer_429_rate_by_tenant -> alert if > 0.1% sustained.
Links: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/alloc/reserved-pool-headroom, https://sentry.redwood.internal/issue/ALC-7604
postmortem_actions:
- Short-term (P0): Deploy hotfixes and widen safety headroom for critical tenants (complete).
- Mid-term (P1): Add integration tests for synchronized microbursts in allocator CI.
- Long-term (P2): Rework the priority dampening design to separate steady-state fairness vs burst accounting; add formal property tests.
- Product: Update Dedicated runbook to include a fast cache-invalidation play for capacity estimates.
Owners: Sofia (design doc for dampening), Jonah (allocator CI), Priya (runbook update).
